newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cen. bank chief sees no overheated economy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cen. bank chief sees no overheated economy.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said policy-makers would continue to lower interest rates next month because there were no signs of an overheating economy, Gazeta Mercantil reported.

"We don't see demand getting out of control, and any attempt to put the brakes on economic growth to benefit the export sector will be very disruptive, which would not be appropriate now," Loyola told Gazeta in an interview.

Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee will meet Wednesday to set the Central Bank's basic monthly interest rate, known as the TBC, for February. January's TBC rate was set at 1.70 percent and policy-makers have been lowering the rate by three to four basis points a month.

Loyola also said the government would monitor the effects of a new tax on financial transactions, known as the CPMF, over the next 15 days. The tax, which takes effect this week, was expected to lead to an outflow in short-term bank funds into checking and savings accounts.
Loyola said this new environment would probably lead to an alteration in current bank reserve requirements.
"We can increase some requirements and lower others where its needed. But it's still too early to say," Loyola said.

He added that lowering some reserve requirements would help bring high interest rates charged by banks in line with the TBC rate. The TBC has fallen much more rapidly than bank rates, primarily because banks have had to charge for higher risk due to a wave of consumer bankruptices in 1995 and 1996, Loyola said.
